A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HeadsUp, with the same core method and experiments. All 34 pages of v1 and 39 pages of v3, including their appendices, support comparison through text extraction and visual inspection.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction experiments on Internal10K and Ava-256, quantitative ablations, inference timings, and downstream generation and animation results.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds a FastGHA comparison, additional qualitative demonstrations, and a synthetic-image generalization example.

M1.justification: The proposed UV Gaussian representation, encoder and decoders, losses, two-stage training, diffusion generation, and latent animation procedures are retained. Additional template and blendshape information documents existing components. The background-channel table correction agrees with architectural text already present in v1.

E1.justification: Internal10K and Ava-256 coverage remains unchanged. V3 Appendix F adds one reconstruction example using an AI-generated image and the existing monocular model, extending evaluation beyond captured studio images without establishing a broad in-the-wild benchmark.

E2.justification: V3 adds a modified FastGHA reimplementation alongside Avat3r in the four-view, half-resolution Internal10K comparison (Table B.2 and Figure B.1). V1 cited FastGHA but did not report an evaluated comparison against it. Existing Avat3r comparisons remain.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported Internal10K validation sample count from '100 frames from 50 validation subjects' to 20 frames per subject. This reconciles the main text with v1 Appendix F.4 rather than establishing changed sampling or a rerun. The established splits, metrics, and HeadsUp training budgets otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 adds a foreground/background separation diagnostic showing where rig lights are represented (Figure D.4) and an exploratory distribution-shift case using a synthetic image (Appendix F). The existing quantitative ablations are retained unchanged, moving from Table B.2 to Table C.3.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for its experiments. V3 retains the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes Avat3r's four-view Ava-256 CSIM from 0.738 to 0.698. New Table B.2 reports half-resolution comparisons: HeadsUp leads on four metrics but has lower SSIM than both baselines. Its PSNR 26.51, LPIPS 0.135, and AKD 3.91 already appeared in v1's ablation. V3 also adds qualitative outputs and a 65 FPS MacBook Pro animation result.

T1.justification: The representation equations, Gaussian attribute mappings, training objective, and multi-scale perceptual-loss formula are unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and v3 adds no formal derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about scalable feed-forward reconstruction, compact UV Gaussians, high-fidelity rendering, scaling behavior, and downstream generation and animation. Added appendix evidence does not redefine those core contributions.

C2.justification: V3 explicitly limits background separation to a fixed-background rig and excludes arbitrary in-the-wild background removal. Appendix F qualifies its synthetic-image result as preliminary and acknowledges inadequate robustness to arbitrary inputs. Appendix E.3 additionally claims template-topology flexibility, without reporting a FLAME evaluation.

D1.justification: V3 documents FastGHA adaptations and training, neutral-latent extraction, the internal UV template, 51 tracked blendshapes, and an 82M parameter count. It adds an explicit project webpage link. Table I.4 corrects background feature dimension from 512 to 256, matching v1's architectural description; these disclosures do not establish changes to HeadsUp's implementation.

R1.justification: V3 adds MATCH and distinguishes its direct UV-texture prediction from HeadsUp's latent aggregation. Additional citations support the FastGHA components, synthetic-image source, and FlashWorld efficiency discussion. Avat3r's updated publication reference denotes the same work, rather than a new citation or comparator.

P1.justification: The main narrative remains largely intact, with grammatical edits, an updated author list, and removal of the keyword line. The appendix moves Avat3r implementation details from D to B.1, groups baseline comparisons, and adds focused visualization and generalization subsections.

P2.justification: V3 adds Table B.2 and figures for baseline outputs, background separation, additional expression transfers, and synthetic-image reconstruction. Existing main figures and ablation displays remain, with appendix figures and tables renumbered and relocated. The hyperparameter table is repaginated without a broader visual redesign.

improvement.justification: V3 modestly strengthens the evidence beyond v1's Avat3r-only comparisons and improves transparency through explicit applicability limits, implementation disclosures, and corrected inconsistencies. The gains are limited: FastGHA is substantially adapted, the generalization demonstration uses one synthetic image, and the new video-generator speed comparisons lack matched tasks and settings. The core method and established experimental findings remain stable.
